chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha, from Muthanna, from Ismail al-Ja'far, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Religion which there is no leeway for the servants to be ignorant of it. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Religion is vast but the Kharijites narrowed it upon themselves due to their ignorance.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you (peace be upon him)! Can I narrate to you (peace be upon him) with my Religion which I am upon?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. So I said, 'I testify that there is no god except for Allah (exalted is He), and I testify that Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) is His servant and His Messenger, and I acknowledge with whatever he came with from the Presence of Allah (exalted is He), and I befriend you (peace be upon him) and disavow from your enemies and the ones who stay away from your rights and are ordering upon you and are oppressing you of your rights.'

So he (peace be upon him) said: 'You are not ignorant of anything. It is, by Allah, that which we are upon.' I said, 'So would anyone be safe if he does not recognise this matter (Al-Wilayah)?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except for the weak ones (of understanding).' I said, 'Who are they?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Your womenfolk and your children.'
Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'What is your view of Umm Ayman, for I testify that she is from the inhabitants of the Paradise, and she did not recognise what you are upon.'
ai.seo_question: Who are considered the 'weak ones' excused from full religious knowledge in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the theological principle of 'ease in religion' by distinguishing between the comprehensive knowledge required for leadership and the simplified faith sufficient for the general populace. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates Ismail al-Ju'fi’s concise creed of Shahadah, Wilayah, and Bara'ah, identifying women and children as the 'weak ones' (al-mustad'afin) excused from deep theological scrutiny, using Umm Ayman as a precedent for this leniency. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that while Imamate and Wilayah are central, the burden of detailed knowledge is not equally imposed on all believers.
